# Stage 2 supplement: what the learned model learned about the trend (generated by probe_stage2.py)

The 15 Stage 2 learned models were retrained with the same data and seeds. Each reproduces its published test cost (largest difference 0.0e+00 bps). Probes use 2,000 fresh simulated hours for fitting (seed 404) and 2,000 for scoring (seed 505); in simulation the hidden trend is known. Runtime 1815 s.

## 1. Is the trend recoverable from the model's memory?

R² of the true hidden trend (1 = perfect). Memory rows use a linear readout fitted on the fitting hours. The true model's Kalman estimate is the best achievable from the observations.

| Source | Trend R² |
|---|---|
| True model (best achievable) | 0.729 |
| Fitted classical model, 50 training hours | 0.728 [0.728, 0.729] |
| Fitted classical model, 200 training hours | 0.729 [0.728, 0.729] |
| Fitted classical model, 1,000 training hours | 0.729 [0.729, 0.729] |
| Learned model's memory, 50 training hours | 0.728 [0.727, 0.728] |
| Learned model's memory, 200 training hours | 0.727 [0.726, 0.728] |
| Learned model's memory, 1,000 training hours | 0.728 [0.728, 0.728] |
| **Untrained network's memory (control, 5 networks)** | **0.728 [0.727, 0.728]** |
| Latest 10 signals | 0.724 |
| Latest 3 signals | 0.688 |
| Latest signal only | 0.504 |

Mean [min, max] over the 5 runs. If an untrained network's memory scores as high as a trained one, the probe cannot show what training added.

## 2. Does the model use the trend correctly?

The learned model's forecasts compared with the true model's, at decision minutes whose next 30 minutes end before the deadline. Size: regression slope on the true forecast (1 = right size, below 1 = too timid, above 1 = too bold). Relative error: mean squared distance from the true 30-minute forecast divided by the true forecast's mean square (0 = identical). Own trend estimate: R² of the model's 1-minute price forecast as an estimate of the current trend. Mean [min, max] over runs.

| Training hours | 30-min forecast: correlation | Size | Relative error | Size at 1 / 10 / 20 / 30 min ahead | Own trend estimate R² |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 0.836 [0.730, 0.910] | 0.83 [0.23, 1.60] | 0.52 [0.21, 0.89] | 0.46 / 0.89 / 0.81 / 0.96 | 0.36 [-0.06, 0.69] |
| 200 | 0.962 [0.937, 0.997] | 0.95 [0.62, 1.27] | 0.13 [0.01, 0.19] | 0.91 / 0.91 / 1.04 / 1.08 | 0.62 [0.58, 0.69] |
| 1,000 | 0.985 [0.951, 0.998] | 1.06 [0.99, 1.16] | 0.04 [0.01, 0.10] | 0.98 / 1.07 / 1.09 / 1.20 | 0.68 [0.65, 0.71] |

## 3. What explains the decision cost? (exploratory)

Spearman rank correlation across the 15 models between each measure and the model's cost above the true model + planner on the Stage 2 test hours (seed 303). The training sets are nested within runs, so the models are not fully independent.

| Measure | Spearman | p-value |
|---|---:|---:|
| Relative error of the 30-min forecast | +0.73 | 0.002 |
| Correlation of the 30-min forecast | -0.68 | 0.005 |
| Size error of the 30-min forecast, abs(size - 1) | +0.54 | 0.037 |
| Own trend estimate R² | -0.71 | 0.003 |
| Memory probe R² | -0.10 | 0.713 |
